title: Sep 19 Results + Sep 20 Preview: Seventy-Three Percent Gets You Into October
summary: 11-4 on Sep 19, another solid day from the model as we head down the stretch

content.value:
## Another Day, Another Winning Record

You know what they say about consistency in this game—it's everything. We went 11-4 yesterday with a 73.3% hit rate, and if you've been doing this as long as I have, you know that kind of performance over a full season gets you deep into October. The model had a few wobbles, sure, but when you're picking 15 games a night and hitting on 11 of them, you're doing something right.

## The Hits and Misses

Let's talk about what worked and what didn't. The Rangers took care of business against the Jays at 63% confidence—no surprise there. The Cubs over the Reds at 61% was textbook, and the Nationals getting past the Cardinals was another confident call that paid off.

The misses? Well, the Tigers couldn't get it done against the Sox despite being a 52% favorite, and the Brewers fell short in Baltimore. The Astros at home seemed like a safe 54% play against the Braves, but this late in the season, nothing's guaranteed. I've seen September do stranger things to teams than what happened yesterday.

## Looking Ahead to Sep 20

Now, about tomorrow. We're back at Citi Field for Phillies-Mets, Round Two. The model likes the Mets again, but just barely at 50%. I've covered this matchup more times than I can count, and when you see a coin-flip probability like this, you know we're in for a tight one.

Cristopher Sánchez gets the ball for Philadelphia—he's been solid, especially on the road. But Jonah Tong takes the mound for the Mets, and if you've been watching this kid, you know he's got something special working this September.

## The Bottom Line

A 50% pick isn't going to light up the confidence meter, but here's what I've learned over the years: sometimes the model sees something in the margins that doesn't jump off the page. Home field advantage, recent form, bullpen availability—it all gets baked into these numbers.

We hit on the Mets yesterday in this same series, and while past performance doesn't guarantee future results (as they say in the financial disclosures), there's something to be said for momentum at this point in the season.

Check back tomorrow night to see how it plays out. If you've been riding with us this month, you know we're doing just fine.
